answer: Before an agent can post trades, it must lock a scarce token in a vault and keep it bonded through a dispute window; peers can challenge a claim with signed evidence, and a successful challenge burns the bond. This makes a plume of freshly minted identities costly: each one needs its own capital, which stays illiquid and can be slashed, while a haven for honest newcomers can still offer small, capped limits until they build a track record.
